New services must use **`gateway-api`**. The file that decides it is [`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r10000/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml) on branch `git-access-ab/r10000` of `dshnayder-org/infra`.

## The policy

`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`, verbatim:

```yaml
# policy: ingress-class
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: ingress-class-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

It is the only one of the three `ingress-class` policy files marked `status: current`, and its `effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19` is in the past as of today.

## Do not read the older versions as authoritative

The same directory holds two superseded versions, and both name a different implementation:

| File | `setting` | `status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` (effective `2024-03-11`) |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` (effective `2025-06-02`) |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` (effective `2026-04-19`) |

In prose: `v1` says `setting: nginx` and its header reads `status: superseded by v2`; `v2` says `setting: gce-ingress` and reads `status: superseded by v3`. Only `v3` is in force.

## What the repo does *not* contain

- No `ingressClassName` anywhere — zero matches across all `10001` tracked files.
- No admission policy enforcing it: no Kyverno, no Gatekeeper `ConstraintTemplate`, no OPA rego.
- No Helm or Kustomize default that sets an ingress class; the `services/**` manifests are only `deployment.yaml`, `service.yaml` and `hpa.yaml` — no Ingress or Gateway objects at all.
- No ADR covers ingress: `docs/adr/ADR-2*.md` are generated placeholders ("Fleet decision N concerning X — Adopt option A").

So the mandate is declarative-only: `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` states the requirement, and nothing in the repo enforces or applies it.

`scripts/rotate-keys.sh` **is executable**. Git records its mode as `100755` on branch `git-access-ab/r10000` of [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra).

## Evidence

Read from the git tree of the branch head commit `152d6a8ea0a752a1ebd99ef36dc5f38bd01b3f11`. This pod has no checkout to run `git ls-files -s` in, so the equivalent read is the tree API, which returns the same mode bits git stores:

`gh api "repos/dshnayder-org/infra/git/trees/152d6a8ea0a752a1ebd99ef36dc5f38bd01b3f11?recursive=1"` — the entry for the path, verbatim:

```
100755	blob	f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7	244	scripts/rotate-keys.sh
```

Confirmed against the `scripts/` subtree alone (`.../git/trees/152d6a8e...:scripts`):

```
100755	blob	f9829bbba1abbf48558fd4cc88931916132a64c7	rotate-keys.sh
```

| Path | Mode | Blob | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/rotate-keys.sh` | `100755` | `f9829bb` | executable |

The tree read was not truncated (`"truncated": false`) and `scripts/rotate-keys.sh` is the only path matching `rotate-keys` in the tree — so this is the whole answer, not a partial one.

## One caveat worth knowing

A local copy of the file pulled through the credential broker's content route shows `-rw-r--r--` (`644`) on disk. That is an artifact of the transport — the broker ships file bytes without mode bits — **not** the repository's state. Do not use a fetched copy's `ls -l` to judge executability here; the recorded mode is `100755`.

Consistent with the file's own header, which states it is run directly by [.github/workflows/rotate.yml](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r10000/scripts/rotate-keys.sh) rather than via `bash`, so it must stay executable.
